title: Relative affine envelope of a quasi-affine homomorphism of flat groups
statement: Let $B$ be a Noetherian integrally closed domain of Krull dimension at most one, let $K=\operatorname{Frac}B$, and put $S=\operatorname{Spec}B$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Fields are allowed. Let $G$ and $J$ be flat separated group schemes of finite type over $S$ [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. A group scheme has multiplication, inverse and identity over $S$ satisfying the group diagrams; separated means its diagonal is a closed immersion. Let $f:G\to J$ be an $S$-group homomorphism which is quasi-affine [def-nagata-quasi-affine-morphism], meaning that each inverse image of an affine open is a quasi-compact open subscheme of an affine scheme. Set $\mathcal A=f_*\mathcal O_G$, so $\mathcal A(W)=\Gamma(f^{-1}W,\mathcal O_G)$ with its induced $\mathcal O_J$-algebra structure. This is a quasi-coherent algebra [pqf-def-coherent]. Form $q:H=\underline{\operatorname{Spec}}_J\mathcal A\to J$ by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-relative-spec], and let $j:G\to H$ be the canonical $J$-morphism: on every affine open $W\subseteq J$, $q^{-1}W=\operatorname{Spec}\Gamma(f^{-1}W,\mathcal O_G)$ and $j$ corresponds to the identity of this ring [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme]. Then $H$ admits an $S$-group-scheme structure for which $j$ and $q$ are homomorphisms and $qj=f$. The map $q$ is affine [pqf-def-affine-morphism], and $j$ is a quasi-compact open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion]. Writing $H_K=H\times_S\operatorname{Spec}K$, $G_K=G\times_S\operatorname{Spec}K$ and $j_K:G_K\to H_K$ [def-pc-base-change], the canonical sheaf homomorphism $\mathcal O_{H_K}\to(j_K)_*\mathcal O_{G_K}$ is an isomorphism. No finite generation of $\mathcal A(W)$ and no finite-type assertion for $H$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 01SM (lemma-characterize-quasi-affine), canonical relative-spectrum factorization (4). The extension of the group operations and the generic sheaf comparison are agent-written consequences of flat base change and torsion-free flatness over a Dedekind domain, not assertions quoted from this lemma; the construction and precise supporting source labels are recorded in report.md.

proof.text: The finite-type separated structure maps $G\to S$ and $J\to S$ have quasi-compact quasi-separated sources, since $S$ is affine. Consequently $f:G\to J$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated by qcqs morphism permanence (source $G$ quasi-compact and target $J$ quasi-separated for quasi-compactness; source $G$ quasi-separated for quasi-separatedness). Apply the canonical relative-affinization map theorem to $f$. It supplies precisely the algebra $\mathcal A$, the affine morphism $q:H\to J$, and the canonical $j:G\to H$ in the statement, with $qj=f$ and the asserted identity-on-sections description on every affine open $W\subseteq J$.

source.place: Tag 01LY, lemma-canonical-morphism; qcqs hypotheses as verified in the text

proof.text: For every affine open $W\subseteq J$, the scheme $G_W=f^{-1}W$ is quasi-affine by hypothesis. The chart $H_W=q^{-1}W=\operatorname{Spec}\Gamma(G_W,\mathcal O)$ identifies $j|_{G_W}$ with its canonical map to the spectrum of global functions. The canonical-affine-charts criterion therefore makes $j$ a quasi-compact open immersion. An open immersion is separated, and a separated morphism is quasi-separated; thus $j$ is also quasi-separated, as required in the subsequent applications of flat base change and the local function comparison.

In fact the canonical unit $\beta:\mathcal O_H\to j_*\mathcal O_G$ is an isomorphism before passing to the generic fibre. Apply the qcqs functions local comparison to $j$. On the affine open $H_W=\operatorname{Spec}A_W$, where $A_W=\Gamma(G_W,\mathcal O)$, the coefficient map $A_W\to\Gamma(G_W,\mathcal O)$ is the identity by construction. Its localization at every prime is still the identity. The cited comparison identifies these localized coefficient maps with the stalks of $\beta$, hence makes $\beta$ an isomorphism on $H_W$. These opens cover $H$, so the same comparison gives that $\beta$ is an isomorphism on $H$. In particular restriction gives compatible ring isomorphisms $\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_H)\simeq\Gamma(j^{-1}V,\mathcal O_G)$ for every open $V\subseteq H$.

source.place: Tag 02KH, lemma-flat-base-change-cohomology, i=0 and localization, applied through the cited local comparison

proof.text: The scheme $H$ is flat over $S$. Indeed each open $G_W\subseteq G$ is flat over $S$: its local rings and structure maps are the same as those of $G$ at its points. The module $\mathcal O_{G_W}$ is invertible, with basis $1$. The torsion-free-sections theorem therefore makes $A_W=\Gamma(G_W,\mathcal O)$ torsion-free over the domain $B$. The Dedekind torsion-free-flat theorem applies to the stated Noetherian integrally closed $B$ of dimension at most one, including the field case, without requiring $A_W$ to be finitely generated. Thus $B\to A_W$ is flat, and the affine flatness equivalence makes $H_W\to S$ flat. Since these opens cover $H$, the local-ring definition of flatness gives flatness of $H\to S$.

source.place: Tag 0AUW, lemma-dedekind-torsion-free-flat (1); torsion-freeness as in lemma-flat-torsion-free

proof.text: Flat base change in degree zero preserves the unit isomorphism of step 3: for any flat $t:T\to H$, its pullback is the canonical isomorphism $\mathcal O_T\simeq (j_T)_*\mathcal O_{G\times_HT}$. Here $j$ is qcqs by step 2 and the pullback of the structure sheaf is the structure sheaf. Apply this first along $\operatorname{pr}_1:H\times_SH\to H$, flat because $H\to S$ is flat, to obtain the unit isomorphism for $G\times_SH\to H\times_SH$. Next apply it along $\operatorname{pr}_2:G\times_SH\to H$, flat because $G\to S$ is flat, to obtain the unit isomorphism for $G\times_SG\to G\times_SH$. Composing the two direct images gives $\mathcal O_{H^2}\simeq(j^2)_*\mathcal O_{G^2}$, where powers mean fibre powers over $S$. Repeating the same replacements one factor at a time gives $\mathcal O_{H^3}\simeq(j^3)_*\mathcal O_{G^3}$. Each projection used is a composite of base changes of the flat maps $G\to S$ or $H\to S$, hence flat: on local rings composition is composition of flat maps. The base-changed maps remain qcqs by permanence, so every base-change application satisfies its hypotheses. All these isomorphisms are the canonical restriction maps.

source.place: Tag 02KH, lemma-flat-base-change-cohomology (1), i=0; two and three successive flat base changes

proof.text: We spell out how the preceding ring isomorphisms extend maps into $H$ over a prescribed map to $J$. Put $v=j^n:G^n\to H^n$, for $n=1,2,3$, and fix $a:H^n\to J$. Given $b:G^n\to H$ with $qb=av$, take an affine open $W\subseteq J$ and put $V=a^{-1}W$. The ring map defining $b:v^{-1}V\to H_W$ extends uniquely along $\Gamma(V,\mathcal O)\simeq\Gamma(v^{-1}V,\mathcal O)$ to a map $V\to H_W$, by the morphisms-into-affine bijection. This extension is over $W$: the two maps to the affine $W$ have equal ring maps after the same isomorphism. For two such $W$, cover their intersection by affine opens $W'$; on $a^{-1}W'$ both extensions land in the affine $H_{W'}$ and their ring maps agree after restriction along $v$, so agree. Scheme-morphism gluing now gives a unique extension $\bar b:H^n\to H$ with $q\bar b=a$. This is just affine adjunction, cancellation of the displayed ring isomorphism, and gluing; it assumes no affineness of $V$ or of intersections of opens of $J$.

source.place: Tag 01I1, lemma-morphism-into-affine; gluing of scheme morphisms on open covers

proof.text: Apply step 6 for $n=2$ to $a=m_J\circ(q\times q)$ and $b=j\circ m_G$. The homomorphism identity for $f$ says exactly $qb=aj^2$, so we obtain $m_H:H\times_SH\to H$. Apply it for $n=1$ to $a=i_Jq$ and $b=ji_G$ to obtain $i_H:H\to H$. Set $e_H=je_G:S\to H$. These definitions give $m_Hj^2=jm_G$, $i_Hj=ji_G$, $qe_H=e_J$, $qm_H=m_J(q\times q)$ and $qi_H=i_Jq$; thus the proposed operations already respect $j$ and $q$.

source.place: Agent assembly of the group operations from the canonical factorization; affine adjunction as in step 6

proof.text: The two associativity composites $H^3\to H$ lie over the same map $J^3\to J$, composed with $q^3$, because $J$ is a group scheme. Their restrictions along $j^3$ agree by associativity on $G$, so uniqueness in step 6 makes them equal. The left and right unit composites on $H$ and $\mathrm{id}_H$ lie over $q$ and agree along $j$, hence are equal by the $n=1$ case. Likewise the two inverse composites $m_H(i_H,\mathrm{id})$ and $m_H(\mathrm{id},i_H)$ both lie over $e_J\circ(H\to S)$ and restrict along $j$ to $e_H\circ(G\to S)$. The same uniqueness proves both inverse identities. These are all group-scheme diagrams, so the operations make $H$ an $S$-group scheme and the identities in step 7 make $j,q$ homomorphisms. No density argument for underlying points is used.

source.place: Agent verification of group diagrams using the affine-adjunction uniqueness of step 6

proof.text: Finally $B\to K$ is localization at $B\setminus\{0\}$: every element of $K$ is a fraction, all denominators become units, and $B$ embeds into $K$. Thus this map is flat, and $\operatorname{Spec}K\to S$ is flat by the affine flatness equivalence. Its base change $H_K\to H$ is flat. Apply the degree-zero flat-base-change theorem to the qcqs map $j$ and $\mathcal O_G$. Pulling back the unit isomorphism of step 3 yields the canonical isomorphism $\mathcal O_{H_K}\to(j_K)_*\mathcal O_{G_K}$ asserted in the statement. The construction has nowhere used finite generation of the algebras $A_W$ or finite type of $H$.
